title: Belonging to Christ
subtitle: Learning together with humility
introduction: Paul writes to a community divided by loyalty to different teachers. Read how he turns their attention toward Christ, the cross, and the wisdom of God.

hints.1cor1-dr-005: Look for the household connected with the report of quarrels, rather than the people Paul baptized.
hints.1cor1-dr-007: Notice the two questions Paul asks about himself. What does each question rule out?
hints.1cor1-dr-010: Paul describes two different responses to the cross. Focus on the people who are being saved.
hints.1cor2-dr-001: Paul names the center of his message before describing the way he spoke.
hints.1cor2-dr-003: Look for the reason Paul gives in verse 5. What does he want their faith to rest on?

discussion: How can we make room for one another as we learn, without making a favorite teacher or winning team the center of our belonging?
takeaway: Return to 1 Corinthians 1:10–13 this week. Notice how Paul brings a divided community's attention back to Christ.
reflection: What is one idea or reference you would like to carry with you? You can keep it to yourself, share it, or pass.

teaching.title: Unity goes deeper than agreeing aloud
teaching.text: In his discussion of 1 Corinthians 1:10, St. John Chrysostom describes unity of mind and judgment as more than agreement in words. This offers a way to think about how we listen and learn together.
teaching.source: St. John Chrysostom, Homily 3 on First Corinthians, section 2

guide.title: Arrive and prepare
guide.text: Welcome everyone. Use the parish's usual prayer or a quiet pause. People may pass on a question or reflection.

guide.title: Read in context
guide.text: Read 1 Corinthians 1:10–25 in an authorized Bible. Let one person read while others listen and follow.

guide.title: Find the evidence
guide.text: Think quietly, then discuss in pairs. Choose an answer together. Before revealing it, find a passage that supports your choice. Read 2:1–5 before the chapter 2 questions.

guide.title: Explain it to one another
guide.text: Invite a reader, an evidence finder, and an explainer to take turns. Ask what changed their understanding. Roles are voluntary; rotate without recording who spoke.

guide.title: Make a fair question
guide.text: On paper, write an original question, its answer, a reference, and why the passage supports it. Try to find a second reasonable answer, then improve the question. Give it to the leader for review.

guide.title: Carry one idea with you
guide.text: Offer the closing reflection. Allow silence and passing. Use the parish's usual closing prayer; shorten an activity rather than hurry the prayer.
